subject: Temporary enclave processor addition — evidence & timeframe clarification
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@cloudenclave.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New transient processor: CloudEnclave (temp) — need sign-off

Hi Neha —

Quick heads up: one of our platform customers (FinPartner) needs us to spin up a short-lived logging/enclave processor to help triage a data ingestion incident. We can host the processing inside our isolated enclave for up to 14 days; it's a transient subprocessor to handle sanitized logs and ephemeral keys.

Key facts:
- Processor name: CloudEnclave Transient Processor (CE-ephemeral-01)
- Purpose: parse and anonymize intake logs for incident remediation
- Data types: IP addresses (hashed), service identifiers, timestamps, small snippets of non-PII metadata
- Retention window: max 14 days, then automatic purge
- Locations: primary us-west-2, failover eu-west-1

We understand Redwood requires notification for any new subprocessors and supporting evidence for SOC/attestation where applicable. Attached are our summary PSA and a network flow diagram (cloudenclave-processor-psa.pdf, network-flow-diagram.png).

Can you confirm whether this qualifies as a temporary subprocessor addition under your DPA and whether your team needs any additional evidence? We can also grant view-only access to our audit mailbox for the duration.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call.

—Oliver Grant
Head of Integrations, CloudEnclave Inc.
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@cloudenclave.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New transient processor: CloudEnclave (temp) — need sign-off

Oliver —

Thanks for the detailed note and attachments. A few quick asks from Privacy & Trust so we can mark this in our subprocessor roster:

1) Please confirm the exact minimum data fields being processed and that no customer-side PII (names, email addresses, full unredacted content) will be included.
2) Provide the attestation you referenced (SOC2 type II or ISO equivalent) or point to a short-term control set for ephemeral processors.
3) Confirm the purge procedure and proof-of-deletion mechanism (logs or hash verification) that we can retain in our evidence folder.
4) Is there any potential for CloudEnclave staff to access raw logs interactively (yes/no) and if so, what access controls / MFA / session recording are in place?

For tracking: please upload evidence to the shared Drive folder and add HUBSPOT-39217 to the ticket so CS and Legal can link the change to the FinPartner case.

If this is indeed strictly transient (<=14 days) and only processes hashed identifiers, we typically accept an expedited review with limited contract amendment: a temporary subprocessor addendum that references the DPA retention/purge clauses and requires attestation within 48 hours of activation. If you need a template, Marissa can share the addendum.

On our side I'm looping Priyom (security) and Soojin (EU data routing) to confirm technical controls and cross-border constraints.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver@cloudenclave.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 7 Apr 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New transient processor: CloudEnclave (temp) — need sign-off

On Fri, Apr 6, 2028 at 11:08 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Oliver —
> 
> Thanks for the detailed note and attachments. A few quick asks from Privacy & Trust so we can mark this in our subprocessor roster:
> 
> 1) Please confirm the exact minimum data fields being processed and that no customer-side PII...

Thanks — quick security review below:

- Control checklist: please confirm SOC2/ISO attestation and, for ephemeral processors, provide a scoped control matrix (minimum: encryption at rest in the enclave, TLS in transit, role-based access controls, logging of admin access, and automated destruction).
- Access: No interactive access should be allowed without a documented emergency process. If interactive access is needed, require a Just-in-Time (JIT) session with MFA and session recording pushed to our audit logs.
- Key management: who manages the keys? If CloudEnclave manages keys, we need HSM/KMS details and export controls.
- Cross-border: if any raw or derived data leaves eu-west-1 for analysis in us-west-2, provide legal basis and SCCs or equivalent. Soojin, please flag EU-specific constraints.

If CloudEnclave can provide a one-page attestation and a proof-of-deletion log sample, Security can greenlight within 24 hours and Privacy can finalize the addendum. Marissa — can you prepare the one-off addendum template (short-lived processor clause)?

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@cloudenclave.io>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Audit Team <audit@cloudenclave.io>, legalops@finpartner.com
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New transient processor: CloudEnclave (temp) — need sign-off

Neha / Team —

Thanks for the rapid review and clear checklist. Per your asks:
- Minimum fields: hashed IP (sha256), service_id, timestamp, parsing metadata. No names, emails, or free-text customer content will be included.
- Attestation: uploaded attestation-202803.pdf to the Drive folder (SOC2-lite attestation for transient processors).
- Purge procedure: automated job runs nightly; we produce a signed deletion manifest (sample uploaded) — we will also push proof-of-deletion hashes into the shared folder after purge completes.
- Access: CloudEnclave staff do not have interactive access by default. Emergency access requires JIT with MFA and session recording; logs are forwarded to audit@cloudenclave.io and can be cross-shared with Redwood view-only.
- Keys: Keys are customer-managed where possible; otherwise we use a customer-dedicated KMS with limited export (AES-256, HSM-backed).
- Cross-border: primary processing in us-west-2; any eu-west-1 processing is isolated and will not replicate to us-west-2 unless explicit approval from FinPartner and Redwood.

We've uploaded the PSA, network flow diagram, attestation-202803.pdf, and a sample deletion manifest to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-enclave-evidence.

We will stand up the processor on Monday morning (2028-04-09) for a 10–14 day window. Please confirm final sign-off and whether you want a short kickoff call prior to activation.

—Oliver Grant
Head of Integrations, CloudEnclave Inc.
